doc.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023

title: How he charges for arranging
summary: Malone describes the union per-bar formula used for Shaffer and the checks for Renee Fleming and Atlantic.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: How do you charge for your arranging?
Oh well there’s a formula — the union book has a way — it’s by the measure or the score page or something. There’s a way of breaking it down. So it’s all mathematical.
Is it further broken down like there’s twelve voices here as opposed to four, etcetera?

Well it depends on the number of staves on the score and the number of bars, or number of score pages or something like that. I just worked out a deal with Shaffer where it was, everything was the same price and then I just used the same formula. It was by the bar is © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
what I do, so I just multiply it bar the bar formula and that was how I billed Shaffer on the Letterman Show.
“And by the way I stayed up all night doing this one so do I get a tip?”

But I got a substantial check for doing Renee Fleming. And I got a substantial check for doing the Atlantic Records Fortieth because not only did they do the 14-1/2 hour live cable show but CBS did a two hour special that they edited out of there so I got two sizable checks.
